correctness.rationale: With a=A(U), differentiation gives h'_U=C(a-Q)/(A-a)^2 and Q'=B(1-BE/C^2). Strict tilted Cauchy–Schwarz gives B^2<AC and C^2<BE for a nondegenerate positive-rate law, so Q is positive and strictly decreasing. A decreases from 1 to 0; Q(0)=H and Q(U)<A(U) give the unique threshold and both cases, including equality (zero right derivative only at 0). The minimizer increases with U and tends to zero as U decreases to U_c. One-sided Taylor expansion of Q at zero and A at U_c proves the onset coefficient; an open-domain implicit-function theorem at x=0 is unnecessary. For a fixed finite mixture, AC-B^2 is exactly the sum over i<j of w_i w_j (r_i-r_j)^2 exp(-(r_i+r_j)x). The (1,2) term uniquely dominates; dividing by C~w_1 r_1^2 exp(-r_1x) gives the claimed Q asymptotic. Equating at x_* with A(U)~w_1 exp(-r_1U) gives both the U coefficient and the logarithmic constant. The point-mass case gives Q=0 and strictly increasing slope. A bounded independent check solved the two-rate example via a quadratic in exp(-x), reproducing the threshold, minimum, and both slopes. The frozen script was inspected but not executed. Finite third moment is sufficient and gives the stated finite derivative at zero; the verification note's wording 'indispensable' is stronger than justified for the shape classification alone (finite second moment still gives the needed continuous Q at zero).

value.rationale: Right conditioning creates a competition between rate heterogeneity and endpoint divergence. The exact threshold identifies when the observed local slope has an interior minimum without fitting a single exponent. The motion and asymptotic location explain why the second slowest class controls the minimum even though the slowest class dominates the mixture tail. This is a motivated distributional result, not an empirical earthquake-risk claim.
